Please like, share, comment The Oklahoma City Thunder may have won the game against the LA Clippers, but they lost something much bigger. With just 1:14 left in the 4th quarter, OKC All-Star guard Jalen Williams drove to the basket for a dunk and was hit hard by Kris Dunn and Derrick Jones Jr. in mid-air. JDub fell awkwardly, pinning his left leg underneath his body weight in a gruesome, terrifying lower-leg injury. You could hear a pin drop inside the Paycom Center as a towel was immediately thrown over his leg and medical staff rushed out with a stretcher. The reactions from his teammates were painful to watch—Chet Holmgren covered his eyes in shock, and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was seen fighting back tears with his jersey over his face. But the LAST moment is absolutely heartbreaking. As JDub was being stretchered off the floor, the entire arena broke into a standing ovation, chanting his name and letting out a chorus of the famous Thunder barks. Through absolute agony, Jalen Williams looked up and gave the home crowd two thumbs up. videos.caption: the NBA was founded on June 6, 1946, in New York City, originally under the name Basketball Association of America (BAA). It was created by owners of major arenas who wanted to fill their venues with professional basketball games. The BAA played its first season in 1946, with the Philadelphia Warriors winning the first championship. In 1949, the BAA merged with the rival National Basketball League (NBL) and became the National Basketball Association (NBA). Since then, the NBA has grown into one of the most popular professional sports leagues in the world.#foryoupage #funny #trending #viral #throwback

Former NBA star Paul Pierce has made a shocking admission that he's 'drowning financially' since losing his job from Fox Sports. According to court documents obtained by TMZ, Pierce claims he is consistently struggling to pay his hefty monthly payments to his ex-wife and children. The documents claim that Paul pays nearly $30,000 per month in child support, as well as a further $20,000 per month in spousal support. In addition, the 2008 NBA Champion spends around $50,000 per month in general bills, including $5,000 in groceries, $7,000 on eating out, $1,000 on clothes, $3,500 on entertainment as well as 'various other expenses'. The documents claim that Pierce's last Fox Sports pay check came in August and also revealed that his average monthly income was around $120,000. The former Boston Celtics star claimed that he currently has $300,000 in the bank, with a further $3 million in property. Pierce is asking the court to terminate his spousal support payments to his ex, Princess Santiago, as well as denying her $50,000 request for legal fees. The update comes after Pierce's lawyer wrote to the court that the ex-NBA star would have 'great difficulty' paying the fees. However, Santiago claimed that Pierce had more than enough money to make the payments. In a previous filing, Santiago claimed Pierce earned 'approximately $195million to $203m in total NBA salary' and that he 'has publicly stated that during his NBA career he made enough money from endorsements that he did not have to use his NBA salary to pay his expenses or generous expenditures on his family, romantic partners and family.' Back in January, when she made the initial filing, Santiago said in a statement: 'I filed for paternity papers after multiple attempts to resolve this privately. Paul Pierce is the father of my son, King, and I am simply asking for a paternity test so the truth can be confirmed.' She added: 'This isn't about drama or attention — it's about accountability and doing what's right for my child.' Since retiring in 2017, the 49-year-old California native has worked as an NBA analyst for two sports cable stations, both of which ultimately fired him. In 2021, Pierce was let go by ESPN after livestreaming himself playing poker with bikini-clad women as the group enjoyed some alcohol and marijuana. The Truth, as he was known during his playing days, resurfaced at FS1 in 2024, where he served as a regular contributor on Undisputed with Skip Bayless. That show was later cancelled and Pierce moved to another show, Speak, which was also shut down. #paulpierce #bostonceltics #celtics #nba #basketball
